headline: Bristol Arts and Innovation Magnet School project, just over $62 million, accepted as complete
summary: The project finished about $982,000 under budget, after about $1.3 million was returned from the construction manager's contingency and allowances. The state has paid nearly $31 million so far, and the presentation said about $5.2 million more is expected at closeout. Nine policy changes, two school calendars, and the consent agenda were also approved.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda, items 8.1a to 8.2d.
Rescinded Policy 5145.6, Student Grievance Procedures Title IX, as outdated.
Rescinded Policy 5145.5, Sexual Harassment/Exploitation, as outdated.
Adopted Policy 5142.4, School Resource Officer, as recommended.
Approved revised Policy 6164.12, Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome.
Approved revised Policy 6141.2, Separation of Church and State.
Approved revised Policy 1411, Law Enforcement Agencies.
Approved the 2027-2028 and 2028-2029 school calendars as presented.
Accepted the Memorial Boulevard Intra-District Arts Magnet School project as complete, and authorized the final payment request.
discussion: Special education tuition: Private outplaced tuition is over budget by $1.1 million once committed funds are counted, but still under budget on actual spending. The report said 129 students with disabilities need out-of-district placements, up from last year, and that tuition rates are often set after budgets are prepared.
Smarter Balanced results: Literacy achievement was 63.3, up from 63.2, and math results stayed flat. The presentation said the freshman on-track rate reached 89.8 percent, the highest since 2019.

Financial dashboard: The presentation showed a new online dashboard for the district budget, with an original and revised budget of $148,825,885. A public version is planned, and members were asked to suggest improvements.

School resource officer policy: Members asked whether the memorandum of understanding should be part of the policy. The policy puts into writing what the district already does, as a state requirement.

Arts magnet water repair: Members asked whether water problems at the building were fixed. The presentation said the repair cost $1.342 million, with $938,000 returned from insurance, and a water department plan will watch the street.
